passages.text: Zou et al. present HGC, a Hierarchical Graph-based Clustering algorithm designed for large single-cell RNA-seq datasets. By constructing dendrograms on shared nearest-neighbor graphs, HGC achieves linear-time clustering and captures biological hierarchy with high accuracy. It enables multi-resolution exploration of cell types, outperforming classical hierarchical clustering in both speed and scalability .

Grabski et al. introduced sc-SHC, a statistical framework integrating hypothesis testing into hierarchical clustering for scRNA-seq data. Unlike heuristic methods, it quantifies clustering uncertainty and controls for over-clustering. The method identifies truly distinct cell populations and corrects false discoveries. Applied to the Human Lung Cell Atlas and mouse cerebellum, it validated known cell types and detected statistically significant subpopulations .

Lei et al. developed DeepScena, a self-supervised deep clustering tool for scRNA-seq data. Combining a negative binomial autoencoder, nonlinear dimensionality reduction, and self-supervision, it enhances accuracy in identifying rare cell populations. Benchmarking across large datasets, DeepScena outperformed seven popular tools and successfully detected subpopulations in multiple myeloma cells, improving resolution and reliability in cell-type discovery .

Seth et al. proposed an integrated framework combining PCA-based dimensionality reduction and Louvain hierarchical clustering to analyze singlecell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Applied to mouse intestinal cells, it identified 10 clusters and 3,871 biomarkers, including 1,892 frequent markers like Rps4x and Rpl13a. The model effectively detects cluster-specific biomarkers, demonstrating high modularity (0.885) and robustness for rare cell-type identification .

This study analyzed 1,077 breast cancer transcriptomes using ssGSEA and clustering to profile tumor microenvironment (TME) immune infiltration. It identified 983 differentially expressed genes and constructed a TME score based on seven immune-related genes predictive of patient survival. Validated across multiple datasets, this TME score proved an independent prognostic biomarker, improving upon traditional TNM staging for breast cancer outcomes .

Yang et al. applied consensus clustering on peripheral blood gene expression data from acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients, identifying three molecular subgroups with distinct immune signatures . Each subgroup displayed unique gender-, age-, and pathway-specific features, including variations in proteasome activity, T-cell signaling, and inflammatory responses. Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) revealed eight functional gene modules linked to stroke severity and hemorrhagic transformation risk, suggesting potential for personalized immunomodulatory therapies and genderspecific interventions .

Risso and Pagnotta introduce Asymmetric Winsorization per-Sample Transformation (AWST) — a preprocessing technique improving clustering robustness for RNA-seq data. AWST mitigates outliers by per-sample normalization and smoothing, avoiding subjective gene selection. It enhances clustering accuracy and biological interpretability across bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets, producing more stable and meaningful gene expression clusters .

This study used unsupervised machine learning (Hierarchical Clustering, K- Means, SOM) to analyze RNA-seq data from 2D and 3D cardiac differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells. It revealed that 3D differentiation enhances cardiac commitment, and low differentiation efficiency correlates with early expression of non-mesodermal genes. The workflow effectively visualized global transcriptomic patterns and identified predictive markers for cardiomyocyte differentiation efficiency .

This study compares Hierarchical Clustering (HC) and Neural Network Clustering (NNC) using Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) to classify Lahore’s 2020 water-quality data. HC produced seven clusters validated by a high cophenetic coefficient (0.9582), while NNC identified six correlated clusters and four outlier parameters among sixteen locations. The combined HC–NNC framework achieved superior clustering precision (~0.8), effectively integrating visual and computational insights for more accurate environmental data segmentation .

Feng et al. introduce DendroX, an interactive web app for multi-level and multicluster dendrogram selection within cluster heatmaps. Designed using React and D3, it allows flexible visual and statistical analysis of complex data. Tested on

LINCS L1000 gene-expression profiles of 297 bioactive compounds, DendroX identified 17 biologically meaningful clusters, including one of natural compounds with shared anticancer, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects —demonstrating its value in uncovering hidden biological relationships .

Peng et al. developed MRtree, an algorithm that reconciles flat clusterings across multiple resolutions to build a coherent hierarchical tree for scRNA-seq data. MRtree bridges flat and hierarchical clustering methods, enabling multi-level celltype discovery without manually selecting cluster resolution. Applied to brain and pancreas datasets, MRtree accurately reconstructed cell hierarchies and revealed biologically meaningful subtype relationships .

Li et al. propose TSC (Two-Step Clustering), which first clusters core cells using hierarchical clustering and then assigns non-core cells to the nearest clusters. Tested on 12 real scRNA-seq datasets, TSC achieved higher accuracy and stability than state-of-the-art methods by effectively handling high-dimensionality, noise, and dropout events. The method enhances cell-type inference and scalability for large single-cell datasets .

Li, Guan, and Zhou introduce CaFew, a cluster-aware feature weighting technique that selects genes with high intra-cluster variability to improve scRNA- seq clustering. By optimizing the clustering objective function, CaFew assigns importance weights to features, boosting accuracy when integrated with methods like SC3. Evaluations on eight real datasets show CaFew enhances clustering performance and visualization, outperforming traditional feature-selection methods .

Zhuang et al. propose FEGFS, a functional gene-set–based feature extraction method for scRNA-seq data that leverages Gene Ontology (GO) terms. By applying kernel PCA and semantic similarity reduction, FEGFS improves clustering accuracy on six datasets and outperforms seven existing methods. Applied to glioma, it effectively identified key cell clusters and marker genes linked to tumor heterogeneity and progression .

Ren et al. developed CDSKNNXMBD, a community-detection-based framework integrating KNN graph stability with partition clustering for large-scale scRNA- seq datasets. Tested on 15 human fetal tissues, it balanced clustering quality and speed, completing 1.46 million-cell clustering in 6.33 minutes, reducing runtime by up to 99% versus existing tools. CDSKNN excels in handling imbalanced data with superior robustness and scalability .

Chen et al. employed hierarchical clustering on 4,551 SARS-CoV-2 genomic sequences from China (GISAID database) to study viral evolution. Using Ward– Euclidean and Ward–Jaccard linkage, they identified distinct clusters such as BF.28, BE.1.1.1, and BA.5.3, which show unique evolutionary features. The analysis highlights potential future variant sources and underscores the need for monitoring strains with high immune evasion and transmissibility .

This multicountry study analyzed 1,071 stage II–III breast cancer samples using PAM50 transcriptomic profiling. The results revealed subtype distribution: LumA (42.6%), LumB (21.3%), HER2E (13.3%), Basal (16.6%). LumA had the best prognosis, while Basal had the worst. Pathway analysis showed estrogen dependency in LumA and immune activation in Basal subtypes. The study

Choudhury and Ashraf evaluated nine distance-linkage combinations (Euclidean, Manhattan, Maximum × Single, Complete, Average, Ward) for gene expression clustering. Using microarray data, they found maximum distance + ward linkage produced the most accurate clusters. The study also identified pleiotropic genes linked to three different cancers through gene enrichment, emphasizing the importance of proper metric selection in biological clustering .

Zhang et al. reviewed computational clustering methods for single-cell RNA-seq analysis. They classified approaches into k-means, hierarchical, graph/community detection, and density-based algorithms. The review highlights preprocessing steps—quality control, normalization, and dimensionality reduction—as essential for performance. Benchmark comparisons across datasets show that hybrid and graph-based methods achieve the best accuracy in identifying rare and heterogeneous cell types .

Fu et al. developed HCDC (Hierarchical Clustering based on Correlation Differences of Phenotypes) to enhance GWAS by analyzing multiple phenotypes simultaneously. Tested on Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) data, HCDC improved statistical power and identified UQCC1-rs1570004 as a new obesity-associated variant. Simulations confirmed that embedding HCDC in existing models enhances detection of weak-effect genetic variants .

Kitanovski et al. present scBubbletree, a visualization tool that represents scRNA- seq clusters as “bubbles” in a dendrogram (bubble tree). It avoids overplotting, preserves quantitative relationships, and integrates with Seurat in R. Tested on datasets exceeding 1.2 million cells, scBubbletree enables scalable, interpretable visualization of cluster properties and gene expression patterns, outperforming UMAP and t-SNE in accuracy and clarity .

Qi et al. review major clustering and classification techniques for scRNA-seq analysis, including hierarchical, k-means, biclustering, and deep learning–based methods. They emphasize the importance of proper similarity metrics, dimensionality reduction, and integrated pipelines for handling high-dimensional noisy data. The paper highlights how hybrid and nonlinear approaches improve rare cell detection, suggesting integrated frameworks as the future for single-cell data analysis .

Nourbakhsh et al. conducted a data-driven transcriptomic study on pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) using TARGET RNA-seq data. They identified 14 expression markers differentiating B-ALL and T-ALL, such as CCN2, EBF1, and VPREB3, several with strong prognostic value. Their analysis revealed four expression subgroups, validated on an independent Danish cohort, enhancing understanding of ALL subtype heterogeneity and therapeutic stratification .

Palazzo et al. propose an automatic dendrogram slicing method for mixed-type genomics data, integrating permutation-based tests with hierarchical clustering. The technique determines optimal clusters without manual thresholds, improving interpretability for datasets combining categorical and continuous features. By
using Gower’s index and factor analysis of mixed data (FAMD), the approach enhances partition accuracy across multi-omics applications .

Higgins et al. developed stIHC, a novel clustering method for spatial transcriptomics data, identifying spatial gene co-expression modules across tissues. Unlike spot-based clustering, stIHC groups genes with similar spatial expression patterns. Tested on 10x Visium and MERFISH data, it outperformed existing tools like SPARK and SpatialDE, revealing functionally coherent spatial modules confirmed via gene ontology enrichment .

Yang et al. applied consensus clustering on peripheral blood RNA-seq from acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients, identifying three molecular subgroups. Each subgroup exhibited distinct immune-related gene modules, linked to hemorrhagic transformation risk, proteasome activity, and gender-specific immune suppression. This stratification provides a basis for personalized immunomodulatory therapies and improving stroke prognosis .

Mariella et al. introduced an outlier-based transcriptomic workflow for 226 colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines, identifying 3,533 overexpressed and 965 underexpressed genes. By integrating genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic data, they linked gene expression abnormalities to drug sensitivities, including PRMT5-MTA inhibitor efficacy in MTAP-deficient cells. The framework supports multi-omics biomarker discovery in cancer therapy .

Talubo et al. performed co-expression network analysis on TCGA HCC datasets, revealing conserved modules across viral and non-viral etiologies. Low-grade HCCs showed PI3K/Akt and metabolic pathways, while high-grade tumors activated p53 and adhesion-related genes. Shared modules for cell cycle and immune regulation suggest common therapeutic targets irrespective of etiology .

Song et al. introduce Multiscale Clustering (MSC), an unsupervised, resolutionadaptive framework for scRNA-seq data. MSC builds sparse cell-cell networks using a locally embedded network (LEN) and applies top-down hierarchical splitting to reveal fine-grained subtypes. Benchmarked against real and simulated datasets, MSC outperforms standard methods in accuracy, scalability, and rare-cell detection .

Zhao et al. present a hierarchical Bayesian model for clustering multi-omics cancer data, integrating gene expression, methylation, and mutation profiles. The approach captures tumor subtype hierarchies and inter-patient variability, outperforming Gaussian mixture and Dirichlet models. Applied to TCGA pancancer datasets, it identified novel molecular subtypes with significant prognostic relevance.

Liu et al. propose DeepGraphClust, a graph neural network framework that learns hierarchical embeddings for single-cell transcriptomics. It combines autoencoder-based dimensionality reduction with graph convolution layers to improve cell-type identification. DeepGraphClust achieves superior accuracy
and scalability across benchmark datasets, identifying rare immune and neuronal subtypes overlooked by traditional clustering methods.
